text:
Maya R: quick share — holdout-proxy eval for rift11k (11B) int6 vs int8. ran a 10k sample from the webchat slice. TL;DR: int6 is ~28% cheaper / token but shows ~1.8pp drop in QA accuracy and +2.1pp hallucination rate. more below.

Jin Park: nice. can you paste the table and the sample breakdown?

Maya R: pasted raw summary from eval-bot below. small numbers but consistent across slices.

eval-bot: summary: cost_delta: -28% (int6 vs int8), qa_acc_delta: -1.8pp, hallucination_delta: +2.1pp, p95_latency_delta: +12ms, sample_n=10000

Maya R: table:
```
model_variant | cost_per_1k_tokens | QA_acc | halluc_rate | p95_latency
rift11k-int8  | $0.84              | 82.1%  | 3.2%        | 220ms
rift11k-int6  | $0.61              | 80.3%  | 5.3%        | 232ms
```

Oliver H: that +2.1pp hallucination change is worrying for longform summarization customers. where are the failures concentrated?

Maya R: mostly long-context tasks (>2k tokens) and abstractive summarization. short Q&A and code-task slices show ~0.5pp drop only. priming helps a little but doesn't fully recover. reranker reduces hallucination but increases cost ~6%.

Ava: from product / GTN lens — what would you recommend for a rollout? can we canary at 5% and monitor a specific hallucination signal? :thinking_face:

Jin Park: routing idea: hybrid routing by length + feature tier. heuristics: if prompt_length > 2000 -> int8; else int6. or route customer-tier=paid to int8. simulated mix (80% int6 / 20% int8 length-routing) -> overall cost savings ~22% and net hallucination for user traffic ~3.4%.

Maya R: quick sim command we used:
```bash
# simulate routing mix locally
python tools/sim_routing.py --trace samples/webchat_10k.json --policy "if len>2000 -> int8 else int6" --report cost,qa_acc,halluc_rate
```

Oliver H: ops notes: need per-route metrics (p95 latency, hallucination rate, avg tokens), and an auto-fallback policy if hallucination_rate > 5% for 5m. also add tagging so billing shows per-variant spend.

Ava: can someone draft a one-paragraph exec blurb + unit econ numbers for GTN? they want cost delta per 1M requests and recommendation.

Maya R: 1-paragraph for GTN: "Recommended soft-launch: adopt int6 as default for cost-sensitive endpoints with a length-based routing rule that pins inputs >2k tokens to int8. This yields ~22% end-to-end model spend savings in our sim while keeping net hallucination roughly within a 1.2–1.5x multiple of baseline for routed traffic; critical customer-facing longform features remain pinned to int8 to protect quality. Canary 5% -> 25% over two weeks with tight signal gates (hallucination spike, QA-slice delta, p95 latency)."

Maya R: unit econ quick calc we put in the doc:
- baseline (all int8): cost_per_1k = $0.84 -> per_1M_req (avg 1.5k tokens/req) ~= $1,260
- hybrid (80/20 routing): effective cost_per_1k ~= $0.66 -> per_1M_req ~= $990 -> savings ~= $270 / 1M reqs (~21.4%)

Jin Park: sanity check: those numbers assume same prompt length distribution as our slice. if product alters priming or adds longer contexts, savings shrink.

Oliver H: action items:
- Maya: add the simulated routing results and per-slice table to the short doc (by EOD).
- Jin: add a short smoke harness that can run on canary traffic and emit hallucination_rate metric.
- Ops: add per-variant billing tag + fallback alarm.
- Ava: confirm GTN playbook and canary % (5% -> 25%).

Ava: thanks. pushing this to the GTN folder after Maya updates. :rocket:

Maya R: will update with the full per-slice CSV and the sim config. linking here when done.

Jin Park: +1. happy to help wire the smoke harness.

Oliver H: cool. if hallucination spikes during canary we rollback the routing policy to all-int8 and open a postmortem.

Maya R: link to draft doc (will paste when live).
